name: Food Products
description: Agricultural and processed foodstuffs and nutritional products for human and animal consumption. Most worlds and habitats produce some of their own food but local agriculture varies with climate, available land, population, and industrial capacity. Interstellar trade allows locations to supplement local production with imported staples, fresh produce, preserved foods, and other products where doing so is cheaper or more convenient than producing them locally.

name: Pharmaceuticals
description: Medicines, vaccines, cosmetics, and other pharmaceutical products. Many locations maintain some pharmaceutical production capacity but specialised facilities and manufacturing processes are concentrated in particular markets. Compact and high-value, pharmaceuticals can be transported economically between worlds to supplement local production or meet temporary increases in demand.

name: Consumer Goods
description: Manufactured goods intended for everyday civilian consumption, from cheap plastic toys to complex gadgets. No location manufactures everything its population wants or needs. Differences in industrial capacity, product variety, and local demand create markets for imported household goods, electronics, clothing, appliances, and other manufactured products. The shelves of the city-malls must stay stocked.

name: Data
description: Commercially valuable information transported between worlds. Information can be copied without limit once it arrives, but nothing can cross the distance between worlds without being physically carried aboard a ship. This makes news, ledgers, entertainment, research, archives, software, private correspondence, social media, artificial intelligences, and other information valuable cargo. Regulations related to CCC Article 54 require the transportation of physical storage media, and guarantees of privacy and chain-of-custody.

name: Energy
description: Stored energy shipped in standardised high-density storage modules. Most locations can generate their own power but the cost of doing so varies with local infrastructure, industrial demand, and available resources. High-density storage makes it practical to transport energy between worlds, creating a market wherever imported power is cheaper or more convenient than generating it locally.

name: Industrial Components
description: Manufactured components and equipment used for industrial production, maintenance, and repair. While infrastructure hubs can manufacture common components locally, specialised production is concentrated in particular industrial centres. Differences in manufacturing capability and local demand create markets for imported machinery, replacement parts, production equipment, and other industrial hardware.

name: Chemicals
description: Industrial and agricultural chemicals used as production inputs. Common chemicals are often available locally but specialised compounds and large-scale chemical production are concentrated in particular industrial centres. Differences in production costs and local demand create markets for imported solvents, reagents, fertilisers, polymers, and other chemical products.

name: Advanced Raw Materials
description: Specialised raw and semi-processed materials used in high-value manufacturing. The galactic manufacturing base often requires materials, processing or other inputs found only in particular locations. Interstellar trade allows manufacturers to source materials that would be more expensive or impractical to produce locally.

name: Luxury Goods
description: High-value discretionary goods intended for affluent consumers. Fashionable, prestigious, or highly specialised goods tend to be concentrated in particular markets. Differences in wealth, tastes, and availability create opportunities for importing luxury foods, clothing, art, collectibles, and other status goods.

name: Military Goods
description: Equipment and supplies intended for military, security, and defence applications. Differences in local production capacity, security requirements, and military demand create markets for imported weapons, armour, ammunition, explosives, drones, specialised compute architectures, surveillance equipment, and other defence products.

name: Compute
description: Computational hardware cores shipped between worlds for industrial, commercial, and civilian use. Compute capacity is always in demand across all sectors and requires highly developed manufacturing facilities to produce. High performance and compact size make compute particularly suitable for interstellar trade between locations with different levels of demand and production capacity.
